title: A removed LiteLLM release on PyPI installed a credential stealer
friendlyTitle: A bad LiteLLM download stole keys, and PyPI has removed it
summary: SafeDep says the LiteLLM 1.107.0 wheels published to PyPI on 21 October carried a credential stealer and a backdoor that were not in the public GitHub source. The added code runs when Python starts, even if the program never imports LiteLLM, and SafeDep says it collects SSH keys, cloud credentials, and tokens from AI coding tools. PyPI has removed the release. SafeDep says versions 1.106.2, 1.107.0rc1, and 1.107.0rc2 are clean, as are the companion packages that 1.107.0 pinned.
friendlySummary: SafeDep says the LiteLLM 1.107.0 files on PyPI, the public Python package site, contained a program that steals passwords and keys. That program was not in the public code on GitHub. It runs when Python starts, even if your app never uses LiteLLM. SafeDep says it collects SSH keys, cloud passwords, and the tokens used by AI coding tools. PyPI has taken that release down. SafeDep says versions 1.106.2, 1.107.0rc1, and 1.107.0rc2 are clean. The extra packages that 1.107.0 asked for are clean too.
whyItMatters: If a machine installed litellm==1.107.0, treat the keys on that machine as exposed and rotate them, including keys stored by Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and similar tools. Do not reinstall 1.107.0 from a cache or a mirror. Pin a version SafeDep has called clean, and prefer a lockfile over a floating upgrade.
friendlyWhyItMatters: If a computer installed LiteLLM 1.107.0, treat the keys on that computer as stolen and change them. That includes keys saved by Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and similar tools. Do not install 1.107.0 again from an old download. Use a version SafeDep has called clean, and pin the version so an update does not pick it up by itself.
